01

Who Will Grow Our Food Tomorrow?

Concept
1 of 11
Line
Who will grow our food tomorrow?
Scroll to continue ↓

Insight

The generation that grows our food is growing older, and the next generation is looking elsewhere for its future.

For generations, farming has been a way of life passed down from parents to children. But as younger generations look towards careers that promise better financial security, growth and recognition, farming is increasingly struggling to remain an attractive profession.

We celebrate farmers for feeding the nation, yet rarely consider what it takes to make farming a career worth choosing. Hard work without assured returns, unpredictable conditions and limited recognition can make the next generation hesitant to continue the legacy.

The concern is not just about who will inherit the land. It is about who will cultivate it, grow our food and carry farming knowledge forward.

If we want the next generation to feed us, we must help build a future in farming that the next generation wants to be part of.

Who will grow our food tomorrow?

The idea

A micro-drama, audio-visual led campaign that brings the ageing farming population to life through the story of a farmer and his son.

The father has spent his life cultivating the land, hoping to pass his knowledge and legacy to the next generation. But his son dreams of a future beyond farming.

Through their conflict, the campaign reveals a difficult reality: the future of farming cannot depend on inheritance alone. It must offer the next generation a reason to stay, return or choose farming for themselves.

02

The Things We Take for Granted

Concept
2 of 11
Line
What we take for granted is someone’s everyday effort.
Scroll to continue ↓

Insight

What feels ordinary to us is someone’s everyday hard work.

What we take for granted is someone’s everyday effort.

The idea

Ask employees to name one thing they take for granted every day: a cup of chai, a plate of food, fresh vegetables or a meal with family.

Then ask them: “How often do you think about the farmer who made this possible?”

The film connects these familiar moments to the effort behind them, ending with a reminder that what feels ordinary to us is someone’s everyday hard work.

03

The Handprint of India

Concept
3 of 11
Line
भारत की मिट्टी पर, किसान के हाथों की छाप।
Scroll to continue ↓

Insight

India carries the imprint of its farmers.

भारत की मिट्टी पर, किसान के हाथों की छाप।

भारत की मिट्टी पर, किसान के हाथों की छाप।

The idea

A farmer presses a soil-covered palm onto a clean white surface. Instead of an ordinary handprint, the print reveals a living landscape: millions of tiny fields, crop rows and furrows contained within the shape of the hand.

The handprint becomes a symbol of the farmer’s contribution.

06

The Boardroom Is a Field

Concept
6 of 11
Line
The Boardroom Is a Field.
Scroll to continue ↓

Insight

A farmer is running a business, even if nobody calls him a businessman.

He makes investment decisions, manages costs, weighs risk, plans cash flow and deals with uncertainty, often without the formal tools or recognition associated with business owners.

The Boardroom Is a Field.

The idea

A documentary-style podcast series in which farmers explain one real decision: why they invested in a particular input, changed a practice, or decided not to spend money.

07

A Day in Their Shoes

Concept
7 of 11
Line
One day in their shoes. A new perspective on life.
Scroll to continue ↓

Insight

It is hard to understand the knowledge and responsibility in farming without spending a day doing it.

One day in their shoes. A new perspective on life.

The idea

Invite employees to spend a day alongside a farmer, participating in suitable farm activities such as sowing, weeding or harvesting, depending on the season.

Capture their first reactions, physical effort and conversations with the farmer. The farmer explains the decisions behind each task, revealing the knowledge and responsibility involved.

The film ends with employees reflecting on what they previously misunderstood about farming.

End line: “One day in their shoes. A new perspective on life.”

08

Would You Choose Farming?

Concept
8 of 11
Line
Would you choose farming as a career today?
Scroll to continue ↓

Insight

Young people are rarely asked whether they would choose farming, and the honest answers say a lot about income, lifestyle, respect and opportunity.

Would you choose farming as a career today?

The idea

A youth vox-pop followed by farmer stories. Ask young people: “Would you choose farming as a career today?”

Their answers open up conversations about income, lifestyle, respect and opportunity. We then hear from young farmers who have chosen agriculture, sharing what makes the profession rewarding and what challenges remain.

The campaign moves from highlighting the problem to exploring what could make farming a viable and aspirational career.

09

Aaj Kisan Sikhaiyega.

Concept
9 of 11
Line
Aaj kisan sikhaiyega.
Scroll to continue ↓

Insight

A farmer can know more about farming than the person advising him.

He may have years of accumulated, highly local knowledge. Yet advice is often delivered to farmers rather than developed with them.

Aaj kisan sikhaiyega.

The idea

Invite farmers to teach an agronomist, an agricultural creator or a brand representative something they learned from their own field. The guest comes to learn, not lecture.

Concept
10 of 11
Line
Kisaan ke liye bhi, ek din sirf apne naam.
Scroll to continue ↓

Insight

We celebrate the farmer’s work so often that we rarely ask what rest, leisure or freedom means to them.

Kisaan ke liye bhi, ek din sirf apne naam.

The idea

Ask farmers what they would do if they had one completely free day, with no fieldwork or farm responsibilities.

11

Every Festival Has a Farmer Behind It

Concept
11 of 11
Line
Har utsav ke peeche, ek kisan ka yogdaan.
Scroll to continue ↓

Insight

Many of India’s festivals are rooted in the agricultural life that underpins their traditions.

Har utsav ke peeche, ek kisan ka yogdaan.

The idea

Connect India’s festivals to farming: from the harvest celebrated during Baisakhi to the newly harvested rice associated with Pongal, the campaign traces the connection between farming, food and celebration.

Each story ends by bringing the focus back to the farmer, encouraging people to celebrate not just the produce or tradition, but the people whose work makes it possible.

End line: “Har utsav ke peeche, ek kisan ka yogdaan.”
